Hi Karthik and Marissa,

Thanks for sending the high-level commitment numbers in the last call. Before we move to procurement, the finance team needs a clear articulation of how a multi-year committed spend would actually roll off month-to-month. A few specific asks:

- Can you show an example of a 3-year $2M commit with annual prepay vs. monthly drawdown (wallet) and how discounts change if we front-load?
- If usage is lower than forecast in year 1, what is the mechanism for crediting or rolling forward unused prepay? Is there a partial refund option?
- How do you handle overage billing vs. drawing down the wallet?

We have a fresh procurement timeline (attached) and ideally would like an example schedule to present to finance on Wednesday.

Hi Ava — appreciate the detailed questions. Attaching a term sheet plus a sample burn schedule that models both the annual prepay and wallet-style drawdown you described (redwood_commit_term_sheet_v3.pdf, burn_schedule_example.xlsx). High level answers here so you can take to finance:

1) Example structure (3-year $2M commit):
   - Option A (annual prepay): Customer prepays $666,666 at the start of each year for 3 years. Discount tier applies at signature: Yearly prepay = 18% discount off list.
   - Option B (wallet/drawdown with annual top-up): Customer prepays $750k at contract signing (covering Y1 + buffer), then replenishes annually. Example wallet is consumed against per-token usage; we show monthly expected burn-rate and an allowed carry-forward cap.

2) Under-usage (year 1):
   - Buffer & carry-forward: Up to 20% of unused wallet can be rolled into year 2 automatically.
   - Refunds: We do not typically offer cash refunds for committed prepay; exceptions can be included for enterprise (> $5M) with an administrative fee.

3) Overages:
   - If consumption exceeds the wallet in a month, excess usage is billed at the agreed overage rate (list minus overage discount). Alternatively, excess can draw from an agreed credit line and be invoiced net 30.

Attached sample spreadsheet includes a month-by-month burn for Year 1 under three demand profiles (conservative, expected, high). It also shows cost per effective token under quarterly smoothing and how discount accrues with larger initial prepay.

Next steps: if this aligns, I suggest a short 30-min call with your finance and procurement teams to walk the sheet. Can you share availability?

Best,
Karthik Iyer

Ava — quick follow up from the product/pricing side with a concrete ramp suggestion you can show finance: 

- Proposed ramp (3-year, $2M commit):
  * Year 1: 40% of total commit ($800k) recommended as prepay wallet. This reduces short-term unit cost and gives you the highest discount tier in Y1 pricing.
  * Year 2: 35% ($700k) top-up at start of year 2. Allow 20% carry-forward of unused balance from Y1.
  * Year 3: remaining 25% ($500k) with the option to convert to monthly pay-as-you-go in the final 6 months if usage normalizes.

- Discount cadence: we can offer an incremental term discount of 2% for each full-year commit (i.e., small bump if you sign a full 3-year vs annual renewal), plus a 1% accelerator at >120% of forecasted consumption in a given quarter.

- Reporting & controls: Redwood Console will expose token-level burn reports and an alert when wallet is projected to fall below 15% of remaining funds so procurement can top up.

I'm attaching an example monthly burn excerpt in the spreadsheet that maps to the above ramp. If Acme needs a refundable or partially refundable clause for year 1, that would be a commercial exception and we can model a 75% refund on unused amounts with a 3% admin fee.

Looping in a couple of brief legal/finance guardrails that procurement will ask about: 

1) Payment timing and revenue recognition: If Acme prepays the wallet at signature, we need to confirm whether the balance is refundable or treated as deferred revenue for Redwood. For accounting simplicity we prefer deferred revenue with carry-forward rules; refunds require an approval workflow and reserve.

2) Clawback & termination: Standard clause — unused prepay may be applied to termination fees. If Acme requires a true cash refund, legal will need to add a clause limiting refunds to 25% of unused balance and a 3-5% administrative processing fee.

3) Audit & usage verification: Acme asked about independent usage verification. We can agree on monthly usage reports plus a quarterly joint review; any disputes can be escalated to a usage verification fixture (hashes & logs retained 12 months).

4) Overage handling: Recommend we keep overages as post-paid invoices rather than automatic top-ups to avoid surprise consumption spikes. Optionally, enable an auto-top-up toggle for teams who prefer continuous service.

If you want, I can prepare a short redline of the term sheet with these options flagged.
